name: ORLaND
full_name: Oak Ridge Laboratory for Neutrino Detectors
summary: ORLaND was a proposed multi-detector neutrino laboratory beside the SNS at Oak Ridge. Its plans included a large scintillation-Cherenkov detector, often called CoNDOR in later reports, and smaller detectors for neutrino-nucleus measurements.
physics_targets: Low-energy neutrino-nucleus cross sections for supernova modelling
detection_principle: Pulsed stopped-pion and stopped-muon neutrinos from the SNS would illuminate several targets in a shielded underground hall. Optical light from charged reaction products would identify flavour and interaction channels, while beam timing reduces backgrounds.

sites.name: SNS, Oak Ridge National Laboratory
sites.location: Oak Ridge, Tennessee; proposed shielded detector hall

status.label: Proposed
status.evidence: The contemporary laboratory and technical reports describe a proposed facility. It is not the later operating COHERENT detector programme.

timeline.event: ORLaND and CoNDOR programme report issued.

collaboration.name: ORLaND Collaboration
collaboration.participants_note: Institutions listed here are selected documented participants; the official collaboration page provides the complete membership.

key_parameters.name: Original large-detector concept
key_parameters.value: Approximately 2,000 tonnes, with additional smaller detectors in a common bunker

key_parameters.name: Source energy scale
key_parameters.value: Tens of MeV from stopped pion and muon decays

key_parameters.name: Facility design
key_parameters.value: Underground or shielded experimental hall adjacent to the SNS target station

results.summary: Developed facility, detector and physics plans, without a completed ORLaND neutrino exposure.

science_scope: The proposal evolved across reports. The quoted 2,000-tonne mass belongs to the original large-detector concept and should not be transferred automatically to every later CoNDOR configuration. ORLaND, OscSNS and COHERENT are separate named programmes.

media.caption: Artist rendering of the proposed ORLaND bunker and CoNDOR detector; a design rather than a constructed facility.
